classification: observed bounded Wi-Fi association, DHCP, DNS, HTTPS and reconnect in Oriole diagnostic Linux

hardware.association: WPA four-way handshake completed with the operator-authorized AP
hardware.dhcp: lease acquired and default route installed
hardware.dns: api.github.com resolved through the DHCP-provided resolver
hardware.https: curl to https://api.github.com/rate_limit returned HTTP 200 after NTP correction
hardware.reconnect: after a controlled link-down/up, wpa_supplicant re-associated, DHCP reacquired a lease, and the HTTPS probe returned HTTP 200
hardware.cleanup: endpoint unbound, Wi-Fi/PCIe/PHY modules removed, temporary firmware path restored, radio absent after teardown

unit.w3_join: experiments/test-wifi-w3-join.py: baseline and fixed contracts PASS; header-only mutation RED under ASan
unit.w2_firmware_map: digest, board guard, partial rollback and init-root mapping PASS

user_journey.scenario: A mobile Agent node joins the user's authorized Wi-Fi, reaches an API endpoint, loses link briefly and resumes work.
user_journey.observed: The complete network path worked in the bounded diagnostic session.

limitations: The test used a temporary private firmware stage and runtime credentials; neither is included here.
The test ran in diagnostic init, not after a cold boot into the normal Omarchy desktop.
The system clock initially required a one-shot NTP correction; persistent timekeeping and suspend are open.
The current overlay has no restricted DMA pool, so this remains development-only and is not default-on packaging.
Cellular data, camera, thermal behavior and a sustained Agent workload remain unverified.
side_effects: Temporary wireless and resolver state was removed after the run.
No Android, boot, calibration or modem partition was written.
next_gate: Integrate the driver and network service into a normal Omarchy boot only after a fresh DMA/recovery review and a cold-boot user-journey run.
